messages:
maria: Heads up — restore of `db-analytics` from s3://redwood-archive failed during decrypt step. Getting KMS AccessDenied on about 60% of objects. Anyone seen this pattern?

encops-bot: Incident INC-2347 created (severity: medium) and alerted security-oncall.

devon: Can you paste the exact error?

maria: log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T08:44:12Z ERROR restore: decrypt failed key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/old-archive-key error=AccessDeniedException
```

ashley: That error looks like the key used to encrypt the objects (old-archive-key) no longer grants Decrypt to the restore principal. We recently finished the KMS key consolidation last week — possible grant removal.

tj: Confirmed: objects in the bucket show SSE-KMS with keyId `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/old-archive-key`. The restore role is `redwood-restore-role@222233334444` which only has a grant on `alias/new-archive-key`.

devon: Quick check commands if helpful:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-archive --key path/to/obj | jq .ServerSideEncryption
aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-archive --key path/to/obj --range bytes=0-0 out && tail -n50 out
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/old-archive-key
```

maria: Is the short-term fix to add a grant for the restore role on the old key? Any security caveats?

ashley: Yes, adding a grant will allow decrypts without rotating. But we need to ensure the grant is scoped (operations: Decrypt only) and set a TTL. Also update audit log tags so we can track which restores used the grant.

tj: Another option: rewrap objects to the new key (envelope re-encrypt) in-place. Better long-term to avoid cross-key grants, but it's heavier and time-consuming for millions of objects.

sre-oncall: For the current restore I recommend pausing and applying a temporary grant. If we try a full rewrap now we might delay the restore SLA.

maria: Agreed. Action plan: 1) devon to request/create a temporary Decrypt grant on `old-archive-key` for `redwood-restore-role` (expires 6h). 2) ashley to add an audit entry to the incident with grant ARN and justification. 3) tj to schedule a bulk rewrap job to move objects from old->new key and validate hashes. 4) sre-oncall to hold restore until grant applied and tested.

devon: On it. I will create the grant using the KMS API: `aws kms create-grant --key-id <old-key> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/redwood-restore-role --operations Decrypt --retiring-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/admin` and capture the GrantId. Will set `Name` and TTL in our ticket.

maria: Please include the exact CLI you used in the incident comments. Also include the resulting `GrantId` and any CSR-like audit fields.

devon: Created grant `1234abcd-...` at 2026-03-20T08:56Z. Applied TTL by scheduling a revoke job at +6h. Testing restore on one small object now.

deploy-bot: Restore job for snapshot restore-20260320 cancelled by @sre-oncall.

devon: Test object restored successfully after grant. No AccessDenied in logs for that key.

ashley: Pulled CloudTrail entry: `Decrypt` call logged, sourceIdentity=redwood-restore-role, requestParameters.keyId=old-archive-key, responseElements.decrypted=true. Add that to the incident audit.

tj: For the bulk rewrap I recommend a two-pass approach: 1) copy objects to a staging prefix using `--sse-kms` new key and verify ETag/hash; 2) perform an atomic rename/move. We'll need to watch S3 request rates. I'll draft a job with concurrency limits.

maria: Good. Long-term policy action items: - Ensure key consolidation runbooks include pre-configured grants for active restore principals OR a rewrap migration window; - Add a CI gate that flags objects still encrypted with deprecated keys; - Update RBAC process so key grant removals trigger a ticket to security.

ashley: One more vuln triage note: we should validate that no human AWS root credentials are used to create grants without MFA. If grant was removed inadvertently by a human, we need to track who. CloudTrail shows `userIdentity.userName=infra-ops`; pinging infra-ops for context.

maria: Assigning infra-ops follow-up: @infra-ops please explain why grant removal occurred and confirm corrective actions. (I will post in the ticket).

sre-oncall: Restore can proceed once devon revokes the grant after we finish rewrap work and validate. Keep me posted.

devon: I will revoke grant after bulk rewrap completes or at the 6h TTL whichever comes first. Revoke command: `aws kms retire-grant --grant-id 1234abcd-... --key-id <old-key>`.

maria: Thanks all — incident notes updated. Closing interim alert; will reopen if decrypt errors reappear. :thumbsup:

encops-bot: INC-2347 set to resolved (mitigated) by maria.
